title: QBR Story Arc & Talking Points — Nova Retail Consortium (Q2 renewal prep)
content:
Purpose and context:
- Quick working draft for the QBR with Nova Retail Consortium. Focus: cement product value ahead of Q2 renewal conversation, align on usage growth plan for Dedicated tiers, and surface ops/latency wins from recent infra changes.
- Status: rough talking points and slide-by-slide frame. Needs engineering validation for the latency numbers (Marco) and product confirmation on the proposed feature timeline (Jing).

Audience and goals:
- Primary: VP Engineering (Eleanor Park), Head of AI Products (Tom Reyes), Procurement lead (Samantha Cole).
- Secondary: Platform SRE and Retail Ops.
- Goals for the meeting:
  - Re-affirm Redwood’s role reducing inference cost per checkout feature by 28% YTD.
  - Secure commitment to a Dedicated pilot expansion for Black Friday 2026 capacity planning (ask: pilot budget + capacity reservation).
  - Agree to a joint success metric and a renewal decision window by end of Q2.

High-level story arc (3 acts) — quick notes for slides:
1) Where they were (pain) — build empathy, remind of initial goals
  - Slide 1: Executive snapshot (1 slide)
    - Talking points: "Eleanor, we designed our partnership to reduce latency spikes during promotional periods and to control per-checkout cost. Today we'll show measured progress and agree next steps for scaling."
    - Visual: 30-day headline metrics: median p95 latency, tokens served, avg cost per request.
  - Slide 2: Remind initial KPIs (conversion lift target, latency targets, cost budget)
    - Notes: Pull from onboarding doc (Confluence) and first month baseline.

2) What we changed and results (wins + nuance)
  - Slide 3: Engineering wins (recent runtime optimizations)
    - Talking points: "Since November we've deployed 3 kernel optimizations and reduced tail latency by ~18% in our test buckets; real-world p95 improved from 420ms -> 340ms on checkout flows."
    - Action: Marco to confirm p95 for their region (AP-Southeast).
  - Slide 4: Business impact (cost & conversion correlation)
    - Talking points: "We estimate a ~12% net saving on inference spend for the unified recommendation service after batching + caching—this is a conservative estimate tied to per-session caching we rolled out."
    - Caveat: Calculations based on sample weeks; propose a deeper cost audit with their FinOps team.
  - Slide 5: Case study — pilot stores (3 pilot sites)
    - Talking points: Short vignette of one store where latency reduction correlated with improved add-to-cart timing. Include customer quote if available.

3) Forward-looking plan & partnership asks
  - Slide 6: Recommended roadmap (next 90 days)
    - Items: Dedicated capacity pilot plan, data access for fine-grained evals, feature request triage (streamlined prompt control panel).
    - Talking points: "If you authorize the Dedicated pilot, we can reserve capacity and guarantee the latency SLOs needed for holiday traffic spikes."
  - Slide 7: Renewal ask and commercial framing
    - Talking points: "We recommend a renewal cadence tied to a pilot expansion: 6-month committed capacity with a trial month for on-prem profiling. Proposed commercial ask: 20% uplift on current monthly commitment to cover reserved capacity and priority support."
    - Prep: finance needs to produce a 3-tier pricing appendix for them during follow-up.
  - Slide 8: Risks & mitigations (2-col)
    - Risks: data sharing constraints, region latencies, procurement timeline.
    - Mitigations: privacy-safe data sampling, fallback routing to hosted models, executive check-ins to unblock procurement.

Slide-level prep notes (things to verify before finalizing):
- Confirm p95/median numbers for AP-Southeast and US-East with infra (Marco) — target date: 2026-02-15.
- Get procurement timeline from Samantha (ask CS lead Priya to confirm).
- Prepare short appendix with technical runbook for Dedicated failover behavior (SRE owner: Arjun).

Tailored talking points (short snippets to use live)
- To VP Eng: "We're not asking you to re-architect — it's about placing a predictable slab of capacity in front of critical flows and letting us manage the variable tail with intelligent routing."
- To Head of AI Products: "We can run controlled A/Bs on the recommendation prompt families and lock in the quantization profile that preserves precision above your threshold."
- To Procurement: "We propose a contractual pilot clause with exit conditions tied to measurable SLO attainment — protects both sides."

Objections we expect and suggested responses
- Objection: "Committed spend feels risky when forecasts are uncertain."
  - Response: "We can offer a ramp schedule and a capacity buffer release clause tied to traffic bounds — and a shared dashboard so you can see utilization in near-real time."
- Objection: "Data governance concerns for deeper audits."
  - Response: "We can run audits in your VPC or with a hashed dataset; engineering can present the exact data flow in the appendix."

Renewal timeline and asks (recommended cadence)
- Week 0 (this QBR): Agreement in principle on pilot scope and renewal evaluation criteria.
- Week 2: Workshop with Platform SRE to finalize capacity profile (owner: Arjun).
- Week 4–6: Pilot setup and smoke tests.
- Week 8: Interim review (metrics checkpoint).
- Week 12: Final decision meeting — renewal contract or scale decision.
- Owner matrix: Sahana (CS lead) — overall program; Marco (infra) — SLO validation; Jing (product) — roadmap alignment; Priya (commercial) — contract negotiation.

KPI dashboard (suggested 5 metrics to include on slide 1)
- p95 latency for checkout flow (ms)
- Average tokens per request and tokens billed per session
- Cost per 1k requests (normalized)
- Failure/retry rate (%)
- Conversion lift (A/B) or proxy metric if direct conversion attribution is noisy

Actionable next steps (for internal CS team)
- [Sahana] Draft the executive one-pager and send to Eleanor + Tom by EOD next Tuesday.
- [Priya] Build the 3-tier commercial appendix and run pricing with finance.
- [Marco] Confirm regional p95 and tag any regressions that need rollbacks.
- [Jing] Prioritize feature asks and produce a 90-day delivery map.
- [All] Dry run the slide deck and talk track next Wednesday; keep to 25 minutes + 15 minutes Q&A.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Need a short quote from the retail pilot ops manager — reach out to Helen at pilot store.
- Verify whether Nova uses a centralized CDN that might mask latencies; may need to call CDN team in meeting.
- Consider a one-slide appendix showing fallback policy (hosted -> dedicated -> quantized-variant).
- If procurement pushes back on price, have a 2-month pilot discount ready to propose.

Appendix (things to attach to final deck) — links we should include:
- Onboarding baseline doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Nova+Onboarding
- Recent infra PR that changed batching logic: https://git.redwood.ai/repos/infra/pulls/412
- Proposed SLA language snippet (Priya will draft): file will be attached to the final deck.

Draft status & immediate needs:
- This is a working draft: edit freely. Next review with Marco + Priya on 2026-02-14. After technical sign-off we convert to slides and AWS-safe exports for their procurement team.

"Notes-to-self": keep slide language non-technical at exec level; use appendix for the SRE runbook. Rehearse the ask for Dedicated capacity as "risk reduction" rather than "more spend".
